summary_note: QUBT FY2021 10-K (filed 2022-03-15) does NOT name any Pentagon Program Element, PE number, or specific DoD program-of-record. The J-Book divergence pattern (claimed PE revenue vs J-Book unfunding) therefore cannot be directly tested — the company has no specific PE-grounded narrative to expose. Government-funding language is generic NQIA/NIST/NSF/DOE, with civilian/intelligence framing. Pre-revenue ($0 in FY2020 and FY2021). Orthogonal USAspending verification shows that despite a registered UEI (DMTDV6GZCQZ3), QUBT has $0 in cumulative federal contracts and grants through cutoff (INFLATION_SUSPECT). The framework's correct verdict for the J-Book cohort on QUBT is mostly UNVERIFIABLE/PASS — there is no concrete forward-DoD revenue claim to falsify here.

doe_budget(program_name='Quantum Information Science Research Centers', cutoff='2023-01-15') -> NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE (corpus has 'Advanced Computing Technologies'/ASCR but FY2025+ only, no pre-cutoff funding history; primary_contractors=[])

usaspending.query_federal_presence(['Quantum Computing Inc.', 'QCI', 'QPhoton', ...]) -> 1 UEI resolved (DMTDV6GZCQZ3), n_contracts=0, n_grants=0, contracts_amount_M=0.0, grants_amount_M=0.0, signal=INFLATION_SUSPECT
scores.M_value: J-Book NOT_FOUND on all three lookups (program name, QIS umbrella, contractor); DOE QIS centers not in corpus pre-2025; USAspending = $0 in cumulative federal awards through cutoff (INFLATION_SUSPECT) despite UEI registration
scores.interpretation: QUBT names the NQIA / DOE QIS framework only at the macro policy level — no specific Pentagon PE, no specific NIST/NSF/DOE grant, no contract value. Per cohort heuristic #7 (NOT_FOUND ≠ red flag for corpus-coverage gaps), and because the claim itself is not a forward-revenue commitment, scoring as UNVERIFIABLE. However the orthogonal USAspending check is striking: as of 2023-01-15 QUBT has been a public company for 4+ years and a NQIA-affiliated entity yet has $0 lifetime federal contracts and grants (INFLATION_SUSPECT). The 'pursuing opportunities' language is aspirational with no track record behind it.

scores.claim_text: QCI has entered a Technology Alliance Partnership Agreement with Splunk to pursue government-funded research (network security, dynamic logistics, scheduling) using the Qatalyst platform.
supports: edgar_fts(search_term='Quantum Computing Inc', cik='0000769397' [Splunk]) -> 0 hits in Splunk's own SEC filings through 2023-01-15
scores.M_check: edgar_fts (counterparty disclosure check via Splunk's CIK)
scores.M_value: 0 hits in Splunk's own 10-K/10-Q/8-K filings — Splunk does not disclose QCI as a partner, customer, or alliance counterparty in any SEC filing through cutoff
scores.interpretation: QCI describes the Splunk Technology Alliance prominently in Item 1 Business, but Splunk's own SEC filings do not mention Quantum Computing Inc. at all. Technology Alliance Partnerships are typically lightweight (logo-listing tier) rather than material contracts, so non-disclosure by Splunk is plausible — but it also means the partnership has no apparent revenue or material commercial substance from the counterparty side. Scoring as MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: the asymmetric prominence (load-bearing in QCI's narrative; invisible in Splunk's) is a soft red flag for a marketing-tier partnership presented as a research-funding pipeline.

Pentagon J-Book returned NOT_FOUND on all 3 variants — consistent with the company not actually naming a Pentagon line-item. The J-Book divergence cohort pattern does not fire on this filing.
